name: Liquidation Preference, Participation, and Conversion

positioning.oneLineSummary: Parses preference, participation, caps, dividends, conversion, seniority, and exit consideration into a state-specific waterfall.
positioning.productLabel: Liquidation and Conversion Lens — based on Feld and Mendelson's public Venture Deals materials
notAClaimOf: ownership percentage determining every exit allocation

attribution.display: Based on Brad Feld and Jason Mendelson's public liquidation, participation, and conversion materials

neutralParaphrase: At each exit value and form of consideration, determine the applicable preference amount and seniority, participation and cap, dividends, and voluntary or automatic conversion rights. Compute proceeds class by class and round by round; do not approximate the result from headline ownership or a single multiple.

locator.value: Preference as downside protection, preference-versus-as-converted choice, exit consideration, and typical IPO conversion
Participation, caps, medium-exit effects, and interactions with later rounds
Voluntary conversion, conversion rate, and automatic conversion in qualified IPO contexts
Q3 2024 sample prevalence of 1x and nonparticipating structures

requiredConditions: All preferred rounds, common shares, convertibles, and senior claims are included.
Preference multiple, base, dividends, participation, cap, seniority, conversion, and event definitions are exact.
Cash, public-stock, private-stock, escrow, earn-out, and management carve-out consideration are separately modeled.
The calculation uses executed documents and counsel-confirmed interpretation.

requiredEvidence.description: For every class: preference multiple/base, dividends, seniority, participation, cap, conversion ratio, and automatic-conversion conditions.
Fully diluted holder and claim schedule, including debt and every financing round.
Bear/Base/Bull exit values, dates, consideration forms, escrows, earn-outs, fees, and carve-outs.

decisionQuestions: What amount is senior to each preferred class?
Which classes participate, and to what cap?
When does each class prefer conversion?
How do dividends, escrow, earn-outs, debt, and carve-outs change proceeds?
What happens in low, middle, and high exit states?
Where do founder, employee, investor, and fund incentives diverge?
positiveSignals: Every round and claim reconciles to legal documents.
Preference, participation, cap, and conversion are separately represented.
Crossover points are calculated for all classes.
All consideration forms and senior claims are included.
Stakeholder proceeds are shown across the full exit range.
redFlags: The model stores only a 1x label.
Fully diluted ownership is multiplied by exit value.
Participating, capped, seniority, or dividend terms are omitted.
Private-stock consideration is accepted at face value without valuation.
disconfirmingEvidence: A side letter changes one holder's preference or conversion.
Debt or transaction costs absorb proceeds before equity.
The actual exit fails a qualified-event definition.
Crossover and participation interactions differ from the summary.
contraindications: Do not calculate with a missing material round or claim.
Do not infer terms from market convention.
Do not treat preference as guaranteed return.
Do not let the LLM perform waterfall math.

instructions: Parse every class and claim from executed documents.
Build the priority, participation, cap, conversion, and consideration rules.
Run a deterministic waterfall over the exit-value range.
Show crossover points and stakeholder proceeds.
Route interpretation conflicts to counsel and final economics to VCFI/Fund Policy.

sourceReliability.low: Only term-sheet shorthand or press-release valuation exists.
sourceReliability.medium: Core charter and cap table exist but one claim or consideration term is incomplete.
sourceReliability.high: Executed documents, claims, cap table, and counsel interpretation reconcile.

evidenceStrength.medium: A multi-class waterfall is possible with one bounded term.
evidenceStrength.high: All payoffs and crossover points are deterministic.

evidenceCoverage.low: Only investment and preference multiple are known.
evidenceCoverage.medium: Core preferred terms are covered but debt, carve-outs, or consideration are partial.
evidenceCoverage.high: All classes, claims, rights, consideration, costs, and exit states are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.low: The instrument or jurisdiction does not map to the model.
applicabilityConfidence.medium: Preferred structure fits with custom terms.
applicabilityConfidence.high: All state-contingent claims are express and supported.

judgmentConfidence.medium: A bounded payoff range is usable.
judgmentConfidence.high: Stakeholder economics are reproducible and Fund-Policy ready.

promotionRequirements: Golden-case tests for multi-round preferences and consideration types.
empiricalQualifications: Market prevalence changes by period and sample.
Exit consideration and side arrangements can materially change economics.
Multi-round interactions can disadvantage an earlier investor despite a protective term.

rights.notes: Public author doctrine is neutrally paraphrased; exact payoff depends on executed documents.

openIssues: Complete fourth-edition and NVCA clause mapping.
Define private-stock and earn-out valuation handling.
